answer: Grading panels drawn at random make sybil rings expensive. A newcomer earns only a copper-sized weight until it has graded peers for many epochs, and the ledger compares every grader against independent panels. Scores that merely echo one cluster of addresses stand out, so a ring can whisper approval to itself, yet the correlation shows up and its stake is slashed. Fake identities end up costing real work that gets lost.
